current.name: Thomasina Blackwater, MD
current.bio: Dr. Blackwater, a Diné (Navajo) physician from New Mexico, earned her MPH in Maternal and Child Health and her MD at the University of Arizona. She previously worked on diabetes prevention and education projects with Navajo and Hualapai communities. She completed her Family Medicine residency at Harbor-UCLA. Her clinical interests include HIV care, addiction medicine, and serving underserved populations. Research interests: stigma in HIV and substance use, stigma reduction in clinical care, and harm reduction attitudes.

current.name: Heather Wynne, MD
current.bio: Dr. Wynne is a Family Medicine physician and graduate of Charles R. Drew University. Born in South Korea and raised in Massachusetts and Florida, she completed her undergraduate studies at Florida Atlantic University and earned her MD from Ross University. She is committed to reducing HIV disparities and improving outcomes through quality improvement and narrative medicine. Outside of medicine, she enjoys mixed media art and caring for her cats.

current.name: Tiffany Yu, MD
current.bio: Dr. Yu grew up in the Philippines and Southern California, shaping her commitment to health equity. She has participated in medical missions in Mexico, Honduras, and the Philippines. During medical school and residency, she focused on HIV care gaps and the biopsychosocial challenges faced by patients. She is dedicated to advancing HIV medicine through compassionate care, advocacy, and lifelong learning.

current.name: Kenya Bingham-Psalms, MD
current.bio: Dr. Bingham-Psalms, raised in a military family, is bilingual in English and Spanish. A first-generation college graduate, she earned her BA in Spanish from UC Berkeley and her MD from the Latin American School of Medicine in Havana, Cuba. She later completed her Family Medicine residency in rural Pennsylvania while raising three children. Her interests include HIV medicine, global health, women’s health, and healthcare disparities. She hopes her story inspires others to pursue their goals through unconventional paths.

current.name: Zachariah Badii, MD
current.bio: Dr. Badii, from San Diego, is the son of immigrant parents and fluent in Spanish. A graduate of USC’s Family Medicine program, he is dedicated to holistic HIV care and addressing social determinants of health. His research focuses on reducing bias in HIV medical education and addressing sex disparities in HIV prevention and treatment to promote equitable outcomes.

careerImpact: Alumni remain leaders in HIV care, research, and advocacy—continuing the mission of serving those most affected by the epidemic.
